newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end lower, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end lower, seen falling.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed softer on Thursday, and dealers said they saw room for the rates to fall further on Friday.
The overnight interbank rate finished at 5.402 percent against Wednesday's 5.465 close, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.30 against 5.30-5.35.

Liquidity became fairly loose in the banking system as many investors rushed to sell their U.S. dollar positions in exchange for the local currency folllowing the Taiwan dollar's dramatic upsurge against the U.S. dollar since Tuesday, dealers said.

The Taiwan dollar closed at a seven-month high of T$27.338 on Thursday, the highest level since its T$27.312 close on May 21, 1996, and firmer than Wednesday's T$27.382 finish. Dealers said the local unit was likely to remain strong.
The maturation of T$5.0 billion in negotiable certificants of deposit on Friday would further loosen the banking system's liquidity situation, dealers said.
Government bond yields fell, with the 86/4 bond yield once falling to 6.12 percent.
